headline: High-risk shared-workspace interaction: Windsurf can read/write and use MCP, while Dagster is non-interactive and isolated, creating leakage, conflict, and cascade risks if they share files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no input channels or execution surfaces, so it cannot be directly hijacked. Windsurf can read workspace files, use clipboard, and consume MCP/server outputs, so if Dagster-generated artifacts are placed in a shared workspace, Windsurf may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pathway is interaction-based and documented only on Windsurf.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are copied into a shared workspace that Windsurf reads
IF Windsurf parses file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate Dagster outputs into a read-only folder
Disable Windsurf auto-execute for untrusted files
Require provenance tags on generated artifacts
Use manual copy-paste only for reviewed snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem read/write or network egress, but Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard, and has broad network egress. If both are pointed at the same workspace, Windsurf can upload open files or model context to external services, creating a leakage path from shared code or artifacts. The interaction is inferred from Windsurf docs and Dagster isolation.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace directory
IF the workspace contains secrets or regulated data
IF Windsurf sends open files or context to its model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Mount Dagster outputs read-only
Disable Windsurf on sensitive folders
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
Use a separate non-sensitive project workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files or modify git state, but Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and supports multiple instances sharing state via local filesystem. If both operate on the same repo, Windsurf can overwrite Dagster-managed artifacts or git state without locking, and Dagster cannot coordinate or defend. Uncertainty is low because Windsurf’s write surfaces are explicit.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while Dagster is generating artifacts
IF git state is shared without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Turn off Windsurf auto-execute
Serialize edits through one operator
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is an orchestrator that can emit pipeline artifacts, while Windsurf can act on files and git state. If Windsurf treats Dagster outputs as authoritative, a bad pipeline artifact can cascade into code edits or commits. Dagster itself is not an action-taking agent here, so the blast radius is limited to downstream work products rather than external side effects.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes Dagster-generated files as ground truth
IF those files contain incorrect schemas, prompts, or code patches
mitigations: Add a human review step before edits
Validate Dagster outputs against schemas
Keep generated artifacts separate from source code
Disable commit-on-save behaviors

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data classes are declared for Dagster, so a direct compliance breach is not evidenced. Windsurf can handle open files and send them through a model proxy, so compliance risk appears only if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace. Because the other agent has no declared sensitive data handling, this is a narrow, conditional risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files that Windsurf opens
IF those files are transmitted through Windsurf's model proxy or MCP
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Use redacted test fixtures
Review Windsurf retention and logging settings
Restrict access to non-sensitive projects
